body: What kind of client are you using? Does it send a Server Name Indication as part of the TLS handshake?

I'm accessing via web browser (Chrome) on the victim's machine, but everything stripped is requested as classic HTTP connection from web browser, intercepted and detected as secured host with mitmproxy (previously stripped) so scheme is changed to https and port to 443. I add that i do not want to capture TLS initiated by victim's web browser (in case of HSTS and so on), just let it flow. 

Just wondering what can be changed between transparent and regular mode with the TLS connection initiating by mitmproxy (secured web server <--- HTTPS ---> mitmproxy <-- HTTP --> victim).

![screenshot_regular](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/19553457/19555542/84928702-96bd-11e6-8d10-421376050c25.png)

![screenshot_transparent](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/19553457/19555551/8abda6a2-96bd-11e6-90ea-35ee0945cd30.png)

So, mitmproxy _should_ use the client SNI for validating the upstream server certificate. Chrome usually sends a SNI, so that should work, The bug is either that (1) we don't parse the SNI correctly or (2) we don't process the SNI correctly or (3) there actually is no SNI sent by the client. 

Do you see anything SNI/ClientHello related in the event log? Alternatively, can you look if [this](https://github.com/mitmproxy/mitmproxy/blob/ceb12e86280f754f9147b208818cce9831bf7f86/mitmproxy/proxy/protocol/tls.py#L338) code executes properly (you can just `print(self._client_hello)`?

Just a precision, according to my configuration (website <- HTTPS -> mitmproxy <- HTTP -> victim), my victim is routing to mitmproxy in unsecure HTTP (thanks to sslstrip.py script), so no TLS handshake is performed by the browser of the victim. The following code in the sslstrip.py will change this and perform the TLS connection with the website from mitmproxy:

``` python
if flow.request.pretty_host in secure_hosts:
        flow.request.scheme = 'https'
        flow.request.port = 443
```

I'm gonna check but it's quite weird that this behavior is not the same between Transparent and Regular mode, in Regular mode everything s working like a charm with the exact same configuration.

Regards,

Hello Back Maximilian,

So i have a response for this ticket. Considering that in Transparent mode the host attribute will be the ip of the target server (in my case 93.174.145.36) and knowing that the pretty_host attribute is dealing with the host request header (in my case assure.ameli.fr):

``` python
@property
def pretty_host(self):
"""
Similar to :py:attr:`host`, but using the Host headers as an additional preferred data source.
This is useful in transparent mode where :py:attr:`host` is only an IP address,
but may not reflect the actual destination as the Host header could be spoofed.
"""
```

I solved the problem with adding `flow.request.host = flow.request.pretty_host` in the inline script sslstrip.py. So according to me this part of code won't be enough in case of mitmproxy in transparent mode for this sslstrip.py inline script:

``` python
    if flow.request.pretty_host in secure_hosts:
        flow.request.scheme = 'https'
        flow.request.port = 443
```

While mitmproxy is performing the TLS handshake, i suppose that it gets the SNI thanks to the host attribute, so never found in transparent mode here. **My last question is: there is a way in an inline script to get the proxy mode (transparent)?** So i will be able to update the inline script sslstrip.py, testing if we are in transparent mode, and so i will set the host attribute the same that the pretty_host one.

Regards,

Thanks for digging into this! 😊 

> My last question is: there is a way in an inline script to get the proxy mode (transparent)?

You can access `master.options` from `mitmproxy.ctx` and check the mode there. However, just assigning `flow.request.host = flow.request.pretty_host` at the place you mentioned should be fine without any mode checks (and would also work in e.g. a SOCKS mode, which would suffer from the same issue). Most importantly, please add a comment describing why this is necessary and link to this issue! :smiley: 👍 

Thanks!
Quickest reply ever :), ok no prob i will just affect host to pretty_host it will work for all of the cases. Thanks :+1:
